Alright, I've just finished laying down the backbone of the Glint CLI core. The series of file writes I've performed—`tools.ts`, `memory.ts`, `skills.ts`, `prompts.ts`, `agent.ts`, `session.ts`, and `compact.ts`—cover all the major subsystems the engine needs: configuration handling, diagnostics, logging, the Groq chat wrapper, protocol parsing, tool execution, memory persistence, skill management, prompt construction, session serialization, and history compaction. The safest approach is to run the agent loop in a headless mode—i.e., invoke the main loop programmatically without any interactive UI—so I can see whether messages flow through the system, tools are parsed and executed, and the state is persisted correctly.

The user is waiting for an update on progress. I should let them know that the core engine is done and that I’m moving on to a headless test of the agent loop.
